answer: A refundable stake bond resists Sybil attacks: each agent locks funds before trading, and the bond is slashed when peers prove fraud. An attacker must fund every fake identity separately, so forging a thousand agents costs a thousand bonds, while honest agents pay nothing beyond a temporary lock. Trust then accrues only through completed, attested work: a new identity is a bare meadow with no history, and it cannot outbid a marble-solid record built over time. Newcomers start in the shallow lagoon of low-value tasks and earn their way deeper, making mass forgery unprofitable.
